age.evidence: FvB/N background male mice (n = 22) from 4 to 6 months old

sex.evidence: FvB/N background male mice (n = 22) from 4 to 6 months old

dosing.evidence: DOI (Sigma Aldrich Research Biochemicals Inc., Burlington, MA, USA) was administered intraperitoneally at a dose (5 mg/kg)

group_housing.evidence: housed in the Psychology building animal facility at Indiana University, Bloomington (no cage density stated)

day_night_flipped.evidence: maintained under controlled temperature and humidity conditions with a 12 h light/dark cycle; direction of cycle not stated

assays.assay_description: Mice freely explored an open-field arena; two blind observers scored head twitches (rapid left-right head movement without front paws) in 5-min bins for 30 min following DOI. Pretreatments (WC 44 full D3 agonist, WW-III-55 partial D3 agonist, or vehicle) were given i.p. 5 min before DOI.

application_type.evidence: Mice received an intraperitoneal injection of either WC 44, WW-III-55, or a vehicle five minutes before the administration of DOI.

setup_habituation.evidence: no mention of habituation to the open-field arena prior to testing

setup_restrain.evidence: The mice were allowed to behave in an open-field arena where neuronal activity and behavior were recorded simultaneously

food_restriction.evidence: Testing performed in an open-field arena; food not present during recording (home cage had free access to food)

water_restriction.evidence: Testing performed in an open-field arena; water not present during recording (home cage had free access to water)

time_to_assay.evidence: recorded simultaneously for a total of 35 min (5 min after the first injection, and 30 min after DOI)

sample_size.evidence: Control n = 7; WC 44 + DOI n = 7 and WW-III-55 + DOI n = 6

outcomes.summary: DOI (5 mg/kg, i.p.) induced ~76 head twitches over 30 min. Pretreatment with the full D3 agonist WC 44 (5 mg/kg) or partial agonist WW-III-55 (6 mg/kg) significantly delayed onset latency (~1.2 min → ~5 min) and reduced the total number of head twitches (to ~40 and ~37, respectively).
outcomes.evidence: WC 44 and WW-III-55 significantly decreased the total number of events (40.29 ± 1.44 and 36.83 ± 1.75, respectively), F(2, 17) = 193.2 (p < 0.0001)

B1_num_measures.evidence: latency to onset, frequency over time (5-min bins), and total number of head twitches

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: the temporal course of head twitching indicated that D3 agonists effectively reduced the presence of head twitching during the following 30 min; quantified in 5 min intervals

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of sequences or transitions reported

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is a drug-induced behaviour, explicitly listed as a non-ethological measure

B5_social.evidence: Mice tested individually; no social component

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Two independent (blind) observers identified instances of head twitching

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice tested individually in the arena

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the open-field arena during recording

D1_continuity.evidence: recorded simultaneously for a total of 35 min

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline behavioural recording reported for HTR

D5_followup.evidence: No recordings ≥24 h after drug administration

judge_notes: Only one behavioural assay identified: head-twitch response in open field. The simultaneous M1/DS electrophysiological recordings are neural recordings and excluded per rubric.
All three candidates agreed on a single HTR assay. Merged into one entry.
B1 set to 1 (2-3 measures: latency, temporal course, total count) per majority of candidates.
day_night_flipped: paper states 12h light/dark cycle and that recordings were during light phase, but does not specify whether the cycle was reversed — kept as not_reported with medium confidence.

Dosing: only DOI listed as the psychedelic; WC 44 and WW-III-55 are D3 dopamine agonists, not psychedelics, so they are described in assay_description but not added as separate psychedelic dosing entries.
